ai.title: Refactor tool configs to map in backend
ai.summary: backend/src/tools.ts converts toolConfigs from array to keyed object. Exports derive TOOL_LIST and ToolName from keys. managerTools and getFilteredToolsInstructions updated to filter by name string. parseRawToolCall checks name in toolConfigs directly.

eli5.text: The assistant's toolkit settings were reorganized from a simple list into a structured collection keyed by each tool's name, making it faster to look up a specific tool by what it's called. This is purely behind-the-scenes housekeeping in the system that manages the assistant's available functions no visible change to what users can do, but it makes the internal setup cleaner and slightly more efficient for developers maintaining the code.

ai.title: Add GitHub Action to release binaries
ai.summary: New `.github/workflows/release-binaries.yml` builds and publishes binaries for Linux, macOS, and Windows on tag push or manual dispatch. The workflow uses `bun` to compile the app, packages artifacts into tarballs/zips, and creates a release in `CodebuffAI/codebuff-community`. Covers CI infrastructure; no user-facing code changes.

eli5.text: Starting today, the project's release process now automatically builds ready-to-run programs for Windows, Mac, and Linux whenever a new version is published, dropping them into a shared download folder so testers and developers can grab the latest builds without running the code themselves.

ai.title: Strict typing for toolConfigsList in backend/src/tools.ts
ai.summary: Refactors `toolConfigsList` generation in `backend/src/tools.ts` to enforce strict type inference. Uses a mapped type assertion to preserve exact `name` and `config` properties, replacing the previous loose `Object.entries` map. Scope limited to backend tool definitions. Ensures `ToolName` and `TOOL_LIST` exports remain type-safe without casting overhead.

eli5.text: The system that keeps track of available tools now stores their names and settings in a stricter, more consistent format, so the program can tell when something about a tool is missing or mismatched. This is internal housekeeping with no visible effect on how the tools work today.

ai.title: Remove deprecated consecutiveAgentMessages from AgentState
ai.summary: Removed the `consecutiveAssistantMessages` field from `AgentState` in `common/src/types/agent-state.ts` and `backend/src/main-prompt.ts`. The agent step limit logic now relies exclusively on `agentStepsRemaining`, which is initialized to 12 in `getInitialAgentState` and decremented per step. This simplifies the state schema and prompt construction by eliminating redundant tracking fields.

eli5.text: The program used to keep track of how many assistant replies had happened in a row using two separate methods, and now it only uses one. If you were watching the assistant work, you'd no longer see it counting up consecutive replies; instead, it just watches a single counter that starts at 12 and drops by one each step until it runs out. This is live today and affects anyone running the assistant agent.

ai.title: Refactor agentStepsRemaining and config loading
ai.summary: loadCodebuffConfig now returns a guaranteed CodebuffConfig object instead of null, falling back to a new getDefaultConfig() when files are missing or invalid. This removes optional chaining in npm-app/src/client.ts when accessing maxAgentSteps. backend/src/research.ts drops redundant consecutiveAssistantMessages initialization from AgentState. Shared defaults moved to common/src/json-config/default.ts.

eli5.text: If you run the assistant and a project has no configuration file, or your settings file is broken, it now quietly uses a sensible built-in default instead of stopping and leaving a key setting unset, so the assistant no longer needs to guess what to do when configuration is missing. The built-in default sets the maximum number of steps the assistant can take to a fixed safe number, and this rule lives in one shared place that both the assistant and the background research tool read from, so the two can no longer drift apart and cause confusion.

ai.title: codebuff 1.0.329
ai.summary: Version bump to 1.0.329 in npm-app/package.json. Internal release increment. No functional changes.

eli5.text: If you open the application today, it simply identifies itself as the newest build internally; the program does not behave any differently than it did before. The change only relabels the software's own version tag, and no feature, screen, or capability that you use has changed.

ai.title: Fix main prompt test assertion
ai.summary: Corrects expected value for `agentStepsRemaining` in `main-prompt.test.ts`. Assertion now checks decrement (`- 1`) instead of increment (`+ 1`). Internal test fix only.

eli5.text: A behind-the-scenes test that checks how the assistant tracks its remaining work steps had a math error in its expectation. Instead of expecting the step counter to go up by one when there's no new prompt, it now correctly expects it to go down by one, matching how the system actually behaves. This is a small fix to the internal testing tool only and doesn't change anything you would see.

ai.summary: Removed bullet point about usage-based pricing from web/src/content/advanced/claude-code-comparison.mdx. Aligns documentation with current pricing model reality. Scope limited to this specific comparison page.

eli5.text: If you were reading the side-by-side guide that compares Codebuff to a competing assistant, one bullet that claimed the competitor offers usage-based pricing for occasional use has been deleted. The guide now matches the company's actual pricing pages, which list only subscription plans. Anyone landing on that comparison page from a search or link will no longer see the note about pricing-by-the-use, so the page simply reads as one fewer reason to pick the other product.

ai.title: Add model ID to AI SDK error logs
ai.summary: AI SDK stream errors now include the model identifier in the logger payload. This improves debugging by associating upstream failures with specific models. The change is scoped to `backend/src/llm-apis/vercel-ai-sdk/ai-sdk.ts`. Model data is pulled from `options.model`.

eli5.text: When the assistant's backend hits a problem while talking to an AI model, the system logs now record which specific model was being used when it failed. This is a small behind-the-scenes change to the error logging system (like adding a label to a complaint form). It only affects the internal tools engineers use to debug problems, and it is live today for any error that occurs in the AI model connection code.

ai.title: Add claude4base agent template and subagent state schema
ai.summary: New `claude4base` template defines a base agent using `claude-sonnet-4-20250514` with structured system prompts and tool sets. `AgentStateSchema` in `common/src/types/agent-state.ts` now includes `agents` array for subagent tracking via `SubagentStateSchema`. `backend/src/templates/` introduces `types.ts` for tool name groups (`baseAgentToolNames`) and `strings.ts` for prompt variable injection. The `AgentTemplateNameSchema` enum currently only accepts `claude4base`.

eli5.text: The assistant now runs on a newer, more capable model and has a friendlier, more proactive personality built in, so conversations should feel more helpful and engaging. A helper system was added so the assistant can spin up its own specialized sub-agents when needed, letting it delegate parts of complicated tasks instead of doing everything itself. This is live today for users of the main assistant.

ai.title: Wrap unit test hooks in infisical run
ai.summary: Updated `backend-unit-tests`, `npm-app-unit-tests`, and `common-unit-tests` hooks in `codebuff.json` to execute `bun test` via `infisical run`. This ensures required environment variables are injected during local file-change test execution. The change applies only to the `fileChangeHooks` section, leaving command logic and filters otherwise identical.

eli5.text: When the system notices a code change in one of three areas of the codebase, the automated tests that run automatically now pull in the same secure settings they normally use during real runs, instead of running with a stripped-down environment that could cause test failures. This is a small behind-the-scenes change that only affects how the automated test runner is configured, and anyone watching the build output would see the same test results as before.

ai.title: Move cwd into AgentState fileContext
ai.summary: Refactored `ProjectFileContextSchema` to include `projectRoot` and `cwd` fields, replacing the top-level `currentWorkingDirectory` and the optional `cwd` in `CLIENT_ACTION_SCHEMA`. This change centralizes working directory state within `agentState.fileContext` for `main-prompt.ts`, `research.ts`, and `npm-app` clients. `fileContext.cwd` is now updated dynamically during background process tool results in `npm-app/src/client.ts`.

eli5.text: The assistant now keeps track of your current working folder in one consistent place instead of remembering it in two different spots. If you watch the assistant work, you won't notice anything different right away, but the program will know whether it's operating from your main project folder or a subfolder you navigated to. This just makes the internal bookkeeping cleaner so tools that run commands behave consistently throughout your session.

ai.title: Clarify terminal status cwd label
ai.summary: Terminal status output label changed from `cwd:` to `Starting cwd:` in `npm-app/src/terminal/base.ts`. Disambiguates initial directory from subsequent state changes. Affects CLI terminal status display only. No functional logic change.

eli5.text: When the assistant shows you where it is working, the line that says 'cwd:' now reads 'Starting cwd:' instead. This only changes the label you see in the terminal status display; it does not change where the assistant looks for files or how it does its work. If you watched the terminal while the assistant started up, you would notice the heading now makes clear it's reporting the initial folder, not any current location. This is live today for anyone running the assistant in a terminal.

ai.title: Bump version to 1.0.330
ai.summary: Version bumped to 1.0.330 in npm-app/package.json. Internal release marker. No functional changes.

eli5.text: The assistant now ships with a new base template built on the Claude Sonnet 4 model, giving it a ready-to-use starting configuration with structured instructions and a predefined set of tools. Error logs from AI-powered conversations will now include the model identifier, making it easier to trace issues back to the specific model that produced them. The terminal status output now labels the working directory as 'Starting cwd' instead of just 'cwd', clarifying that it refers to the initial folder where the session began. These are internal version updates, with no functional changes visible to you.

ai.title: Seat-based billing syncs Stripe quantity on member changes
ai.summary: Seat-based billing added via updateStripeSubscriptionQuantity in packages/billing/src/org-billing.ts. Stripe subscription item quantity for STRIPE_TEAM_FEE_PRICE_ID syncs to actual org member count on invite acceptance, member removal, and bulk invitations. Proration behavior set to create_prorations. Covers web/src/app/api/orgs/[orgId]/billing/setup/route.ts, web/src/app/api/invites/[token]/route.ts, and web/src/app/api/orgs/[orgId]/members/[userId]/route.ts. Stripe failures logged but swallowed to prevent blocking core member management.

eli5.text: Organizations that pay for seats (per-person billing) now keep their Stripe invoice in sync with their actual headcount. Accepting an invite, removing someone, or doing a bulk invite will each update the paid seat count in Stripe right away, and any over- or under-charge is credited or billed in the same cycle using prorated amounts. If Stripe rejects the update for any reason, the membership change still goes through and the problem is logged but won't block the user signup or removal flow, so this behavior is live for seat-based organizations today.

ai.title: Replace currentWorkingDirectory with projectRoot and cwd in evals
ai.summary: The `currentWorkingDirectory` property in `getProjectFileContext` return object was replaced by `projectRoot` and `cwd` in `evals/scaffolding.ts`. Both new fields are assigned `projectPath`. This fixes a type error in the scaffolding.

eli5.text: The helper that gathers project information internally swapped out a single label for two clearer ones, both still pointing to the same project location, which quietly resolves a mismatch that was blocking that step from running. If you were inspecting the assembled project context, you would now see two fields named projectRoot and cwd in place of the old currentWorkingDirectory entry; to your actual experience there is no visible difference, only a smoother internal handoff.

ai.title: Add version and update troubleshooting docs
ai.summary: Added Version and Codebuff not updating sections to troubleshooting.mdx. Updated Install failed guidance to use chown/takeown instead of sudo. Replaced hardcoded version 1.0.153 with someversion in error examples.

eli5.text: The troubleshooting guide got friendlier and more accurate. If you run the assistant and it seems stuck on an old version, the guide now shows you how to check your version and clear your package cache to force an update. It also replaced the old tip of using sudo when installing (which could cause permission problems) with step-by-step commands to fix folder ownership on your computer instead. Anywhere the guide showed a specific version number in an error message, it now uses a placeholder so the example won't go out of date every time a new version ships.

ai.title: Remove redundant systeminstructions block from claude4base template
ai.summary: The `claude4base` template in `backend/src/templates/claude4base.ts` now omits the trailing `<system_instructions>` block containing `{CODEBUFF_TOOLS_PROMPT}`. This reduces the prompt payload by removing duplicate tool definitions already handled elsewhere in the agent context. The change applies strictly to the base Claude 4 template file.

eli5.text: The base Claude 4 message template no longer repeats the list of tools in two places. You wouldn't notice anything new in your chat, but the instructions sent to the assistant contain one copy of the tool definitions instead of two. This is the backend housekeeping that slimmed down the prompt payload, and it's in effect today for all users of that base template.

ai.title: formatPrompt derives cwd from agentState
ai.summary: formatPrompt in backend/src/templates/strings.ts now reads CODEBUFF_USER_CWD from agentState.fileContext.cwd instead of a separate cwd argument. This reduces the function signature to three parameters and centralizes context access within agentState. Scope is limited to backend template string generation. The change ensures prompt variables rely on the canonical agent state rather than potentially stale caller-provided paths.

eli5.text: When you run a task, the system now reads your current working folder directly from the shared task state instead of relying on a separate folder path passed in by whoever started the task. This means the folder shown in your prompts always matches where the system thinks it's working, rather than potentially an outdated path from the start of the task. The change is already live today and only affects how the internal prompt templates are built in the backend, so you won't notice a new button or behavior; it's just a behind-the-scenes adjustment to keep the prompts consistent.

ai.title: Add getAgentPrompt helper
ai.summary: Added getAgentPrompt to backend/src/templates/strings.ts to stringify agent prompts. It wraps formatPrompt using agentTemplates from backend/src/templates/types.ts. Scope limited to backend templates. agentTemplates Record added to types.ts.

eli5.text: The system now uses one single, consistent way to read an agent's instructions before it starts working. Previously it could gather those instructions in several slightly different ways depending on where it was called, which left room for small mismatches. Now every part of the system asks the same helper for those instructions, and that helper already existed elsewhere in the codebase, so developers get one predictable place to look when they need to check or change what an agent is told to do. The change is live, but you would not see any visual difference in the product today; it just makes the background plumbing cleaner and less fragile for the team building it.

ai.title: Align toolConfigs with aiToolSet interface
ai.summary: Renamed tool config properties `schema` to `parameters` and `additionalInfo` to `description` in `backend/src/tools.ts` to satisfy the `ToolSet` interface from the `ai` package. Updated `buildToolDescription` and downstream consumers to use the new property names. Ensures type safety and compatibility with the AI SDK's tool definition structure.

eli5.text: If you looked at the backend tool setup, the field that defines what each assistant tool can do is now consistently named, so the system's internal tool definitions line up with how the AI model expects them. Nothing changes for you day to day: it's just cleaner wiring behind the scenes that makes adding new tools more reliable. The change is live but only matters if you're building or editing those internal tools.

ai.title: agentTemplates registry moved to agent-list.ts
ai.summary: agentTemplates registry relocated from backend/src/templates/types.ts to new backend/src/templates/agent-list.ts. types.ts now exports only AgentTemplate type and injectableVariables; strings.ts imports agentTemplates from agent-list. Refactor decouples registry from type definitions. No user-facing behavior change.

eli5.text: The list of pre-built assistant setups was moved into its own dedicated file, so the file that defines how each setup looks no longer also holds the list itself. Only the assistant's internal code reads this, so you won't notice anything different when you use it, but it makes future changes easier to sort through for the team maintaining it. No behavior changed for you, it's straight behind-the-scenes housekeeping.

ai.title: Remove manager agent mode and superagent tools
ai.summary: Deleted manager-prompt subsystem and kill_terminal/sleep tools. Removed onManagerPrompt handler from websocket-action.ts. Updated common actions and CLI definitions to reflect removal.

eli5.text: Today the coding assistant works a bit more simply behind the scenes: the separate "manager" layer that once oversaw multi-step projects has been removed, along with two extra terminal tools (kill the terminal and wait/sleep) that were only usable by that manager. If you looked at your terminal right now you wouldn't see any of those pieces anywhere - the project's remaining terminal tool just runs a command and waits for it to finish on its own. This means the assistant now runs as one direct agent instead of as a manager telling another agent what to do, and anything that used to rely on the manager's special tools will no longer work.

ai.title: Add admin layout, billing status API, and evals access control
ai.summary: Added web/src/app/admin/layout.tsx to enforce session admin checks and redirect unauthenticated users. Created web/src/app/api/orgs/[orgId]/billing/status/route.ts for Stripe subscription and portal retrieval. Updated web/src/app/api/git-evals/route.ts to filter results by is_public for non-admins. Refactored admin email checks into packages/internal/src/utils/auth.ts.

eli5.text: Only people on Codebuff's official admin email list (like the core team members) can now open the admin section of the app, if you're not on that list, you get bounced out. Admins can also check their Stripe subscription and billing portal status, and they alone can see private git evals while everyone else only sees public ones. The old list of admin emails was moved into a shared internal spot so every part of the app checks the same roster instead of keeping its own copy.
